$comment: Release-only upgrade rehearsal (docs/operations/upgrades.md#release-gate-upgrade-rehearsal). For every supported source release, the candidate upgrades one install per dataset. Datasets are generated by the SOURCE release's own tooling, because a real install holds data its own version wrote. Every class in requiredDatasetClasses must name at least one dataset, and plan.mjs refuses otherwise. Never wire this into push or pull_request CI.

knownHarnessDefects.reason: The tagged harness recomputes open_balance in functional currency (sum of abs(amount) minus application amount), but since migration 0100 the stored balance is in the document's own currency, so every foreign-currency document reads as stale. Fixed on main (R1.10).

The tagged harness probes the base table on its own pool login, which in the rehearsal is the database superuser that FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY cannot bind, so with two or more document-holding orgs it sees foreign rows. Fixed on main (R1.11).

datasets.description: A bootstrapped install with no activity: the default org only.
One general contractor, one quarter of seeded activity.
Every sample-company template the source release can prepare.
Recurring-revenue and services companies over a fiscal year-end.
Endurance loop across a year-end and a leap day, with the adversarial probes: backdating into closed periods, posted edits, over-application, reversal symmetry, void and recreate.

Legacy shapes from earlier releases that upgrade cleanly with notices: a tenant catch-all group (0306 adds the default, 0319 retires it), an executed lien waiver renamed afterwards, an unbound active SFTP schedule, a recognition rule edited after obligations, a rate version older than a profile edit, a retention completion inheriting a live action, and grandfathered posted stock-count history. Runs the full upgrade, then assertions/edge-legacy.mjs.

Legacy shapes that must refuse the upgrade by name: duplicate stock-count subjects and negative counts on draft counts, and malformed payrollRemittance markers. The cell proves --check reports exactly expectFindings, a plain bootstrap refuses without touching the ledger, the remedy files (the same remedy text operators get) apply, --check comes back clean, and the full phases run. Finding counts are seed-pinned (the seeder writes two duplicate groups, two negative lines, and markers failing four field checks); finding keys compare as a multiset, so any seed change must update this list and drift fails the cell loudly.
